research_mode: official ONS, Home Office and Police.uk sources only; repeat-victimisation, sensitive self-completion, domestic-abuse measure transitions, outcome definitions and Police.uk identity or missing-location semantics; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: CSEW repeat-victimisation series definition
verified_claims: respondents identify a series as the same thing under the same circumstances and probably by the same people
the number of incidents in the series is recorded
only one detailed victim module is completed based on the most recent incident
limitations: one detailed module does not describe every incident in a series
series classification depends on respondent reporting

sources.name: Historical CSEW repeat-incident cap
verified_claims: from 1981 the first five incidents of a series were included in estimates
the cap reduced year-to-year sample variability
the approach supported a more stable time series
limitations: historical stability was achieved by excluding higher-order incidents
pre-change estimates are not directly comparable with the revised method

sources.name: Historical cap bias limitation
verified_claims: the five-incident cap could lower estimates for crime types such as violence
high-order repeat victimisation could be concentrated in subgroups
ONS cites sustained victimisation by a partner or family member as a potential measurement-error concern
limitations: the limitation does not quantify every subgroup effect
historical and revised series require explicit break metadata

sources.name: Repeat-victimisation methodology review
verified_claims: ONS commissioned a review of high-frequency repeat-victimisation methods in 2015
the review was completed in spring 2016
users were consulted between July and September 2016
limitations: review chronology is not a measurement result
implemented methodology must be distinguished from proposals considered

sources.name: Current repeat-victimisation imputation method
verified_claims: the arbitrary cap of five was replaced by crime-specific imputation
the maximum is based on the 98th percentile of victim incident counts
percentiles are calculated from three-year rolling datasets
limitations: the maximum varies by crime type and reference period
edition-specific percentile tables are required

sources.name: Repeat-victimisation minimum cap rule
verified_claims: for many crime types the calculated 98th percentile is below five
ONS does not lower the maximum below five in those cases
incidents above the percentile can therefore remain included when the percentile is below five
limitations: the rule is not a universal five-incident cap
crime-specific implementation must be read from the current table

sources.name: Crime types affected by repeat-method change
verified_claims: violence estimates are noticeably affected by the 98th-percentile method
criminal-damage estimates are also noticeably affected
most other crime types show smaller effects
limitations: method effect is not evidence of a real-world crime change
affected categories still require confidence intervals

sources.name: Child repeat-victimisation percentile limitation
verified_claims: 98th-percentile values are more variable for children aged 10 to 15 than for adults
the child survey has a different sample structure
child and adult repeat-victimisation thresholds should not be pooled
limitations: greater variability does not invalidate child estimates
child-specific editions and uncertainty remain necessary

sources.name: CSEW incident-series weight role
verified_claims: the numinc weight is used for calculating incidents
it is distinct from the core individual weight
incident and prevalence calculations therefore use different weighting roles
limitations: numinc is not a general person weight
weight formulas are edition dependent

sources.name: Repeat-method design-weight adjustment
verified_claims: the revised method included adjustments to survey design weights
the adjustments reduce variance in weights
the purpose was to lessen volatility in survey estimates
limitations: variance reduction does not remove sampling or measurement error
old and revised weighting systems require separate metadata
